title: Bru-Seq
scope: Paulsen 2013 Bru-seq synthesis pulse implementation, clarified by the registered PMID23973811 detailed protocol. The assigned standalone diagram and the poster’s middle Bru-Seq row depict metabolic labeling, RNA isolation, antibody-bead capture, elution and cDNA library preparation. Primary-supported fragmentation follows elution. The poster’s GRO-seq/BRIC-Seq and BruChase-Seq rows are contextual neighboring workflows; its standalone cropped chemical drawings at the right are not reactions in this route. The endpoint is a physical cDNA library, with prospective readout explained but no unshown sequencing/data-analysis operations added.

operations.label: Label newly synthesized RNA with bromouridine
operations.description: Expose cultured cells to bromouridine during the synthesis pulse, producing cells whose newly synthesized RNA incorporates the analog. The depicted Br-UTP stars identify the RNA-incorporated label; the primary protocol supplies bromouridine in culture medium.
operations.mechanism: Metabolic bromouridine labeling of RNA in living cells.
operations.information_effect: The RNA-borne label links the selected population to a synthesis time window; no chase is included.

operations.label: Fragment selected RNA and prepare a strand-specific cDNA library
operations.description: Fragment the eluted Bru-RNA, then convert its sequence information into a cDNA sequencing library. Retain library preparation as the broad depicted block. Primary evidence places fragmentation here and identifies first- and second-strand synthesis, adaptor addition and amplification within this block.
operations.mechanism: Reverse transcription and cDNA library synthesis; the detailed protocol includes dU in second-strand synthesis and uridine digestion in its strand-specific preparation. The diagram does not enumerate these substeps.
operations.information_effect: The final physical library can be sequenced to infer nascent transcription and relative synthesis. Bromouridine was the RNA selection feature, not a claimed modification on the cDNA reporter.
